dedupe_keys.name: imdea energy building in madrid white roof solar shading and bioclimatic design climate adapt

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study presents the headquarters of the IMDEA Energy institute in the Madrid region, designed with Arkitools on bioclimatic principles to stay cool through hotter summers and use little energy and water. Measures include a white reflective covering on sun-exposed roofs to cut cooling demand and the heat island contribution, a fixed system of large horizontal louvres that shades glazing while keeping views and admitting low winter sun, back-ventilated facades with 80 mm insulation, large glazed internal walls for daylight, and solar panels built into the roof; soil tests for the foundations also assessed aquifer thermal energy storage. Construction ran from May 2010 to May 2012 and cost about EUR 9.2 million, funded indirectly through the Community of Madrid with national and ERDF research funds; the useful life is estimated at over 50 years. Coverage: one building, set against projections of hot nights rising from 50 in 2010 to 114 in 2100 under RCP8.5. Access: the case study page, published on 7 June 2016 and modified on 25 August 2026, with a Construction21 page. Licence: Climate-ADAPT content under the EEA reuse policy; free. Caveats: the page gives design intent and cost but no measured energy or temperature results. Simulation uses are a reference for modelling cool roofs and shading in hot-climate building energy and overheating studies. Related records: the Torino 25 Verde and Los Angeles albedo case studies.
name: IMDEA Energy building in Madrid: white roof, solar shading and bioclimatic design (Climate-ADAPT)
outcomes: A research building completed in May 2012 at about EUR 9.2 million, with a reflective white roof, fixed louvre shading, back-ventilated facades with 80 mm insulation and integrated solar panels; its useful life is estimated at over 50 years and energy monitoring continues.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study based on Arkitools and IMDEA Energy
